newsitem.title: USA: CHRYSLER SEES EARLY PROFITS FROM NEW SEDANS.
newsitem.headline: CHRYSLER SEES EARLY PROFITS FROM NEW SEDANS.

text.p: Chrysler Corp., which cut eight months off the development time of its new large sedans, expects the cars to start producing profits fairly quickly, a top company executive said Thursday.

Ronald Boltz, general manager of Chrysler's large car operations, would not specify when the new Chrysler Concorde and Dodge Intrepid sedans will begin to turn a profit. The cars will go on sale in October.
"I would guess they'll be profitable pretty quickly after we launch them," Boltz said following a speech at the University of Michigan's annual auto conference here.

Chrysler officials said earlier this week that the U.S. No. 3 automaker was able to cut $75 million to $80 million off the engineering costs of the new LH cars by using refined platform teams and computer-aided design.
Total investment costs for the cars is $2.1 billion. Their time-to-market after design approval is 31 months, down from the 39 months for the previous version.
Boltz told reporters Thursday Chrysler is comfortable with its product mix weighted heavily toward trucks.
Despite occasional minor changes in gasoline taxes, Boltz said Americans will continue to enjoy low fuel prices and want larger vehicles.
"We've got the world's cheapest gasoline, and as long as we do, we're going to see demand for larger vehicles with bigger engines," he said.
Chrysler has the highest percentage of light truck sales among the U.S. Big Three. About 66 percent of its annual sales are minivans, pickup trucks and sport/utility vehicles.
